title: Project setup: workspaces, walking skeleton and CI
description:
As a developer, I want the project scaffolding in place so that every following story can build, test and ship features.

Set up npm workspaces with the server (`src/axon`, Express + Socket.IO), shared contract package (`src/axon.Shared`, Zod), React app (`src/axon.Frontend`, Vite, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Zustand, React Router) and Playwright tests (`src/axon.E2ETests`). The server serves the built front end. No game features yet.

**Scope:** full-stack (touches `src/`).

**Specs:** `.github/memorybank/features/planning-poker/design.md` (Architecture, Project Layout, Technology Stack, Security) and `.github/project-config.md` (structure, commands, test suites).

**Depends on:** nothing.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Given a fresh clone, when I run `npm ci` and `npm run build` at the root, then all workspaces build without errors.
2. Given the server is running, when I call `GET /healthz`, then it returns `200`.
3. Given the server is running, when I open `/` in a browser, then the React app shell loads (app name and an empty home page).
4. Given the server is running, when any response is returned, then security headers from `helmet` are present, including a Content-Security-Policy.
5. Given `npm run dev` at the root, then the server and the Vite dev server start, and Vite proxies `/api` and `/socket.io` to the server.
6. Given the test runner, when I run the `unit`, `integration`, `frontend` and `e2e` suites, then each finds and passes at least one smoke test (`.github/scripts/test/suites/*.json`).
7. `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` pass with TypeScript `strict` enabled in every workspace.
8. Given a pull request to `main`, then a GitHub Actions workflow runs install, lint, type check, build and all four test suites, and fails the check if any step fails.

title: Create a game and join it with a link and a name
description:
As a facilitator, I want to create a game and share a link, and as a voter, I want to join with only my name, so that the team can start a session without accounts.

Covers the in-memory `GameStore`, `POST /api/games`, `GET /api/games/:id/exists`, the Socket.IO `game:join` / `game:joined` / `game:state` events, player tokens, the create page, the join prompt and the poker table showing who is in the game.

**Scope:** full-stack.

**Specs:** `requirements.md` Req 1 (all), Req 2 (all), Req 9.1; `design.md` sections Data Model, Realtime Events, `PublicGameState`, Join and Reconnect, REST API, Security, Error Handling.

**Depends on:** Project setup.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Given the home page, when I enter a name (1-30 characters after trimming) and create a game, then I land on `/g/{gameId}` as facilitator and see the join link with a copy button.
2. The `gameId` is generated with at least 128 bits of randomness; no account, email or password is asked for.
3. Given a valid game link, when a visitor opens it, then they are asked for a name before joining.
4. Given a name that is empty, longer than 30 characters, or already used in the game (case-insensitive), when the visitor submits it, then it is rejected with a clear message (`INVALID_NAME` / `NAME_TAKEN`) and they can try again.
5. Given a voter joins, then every connected player sees the new voter within 1 second.
6. Given a player reloads the page or reconnects, when their browser still has the player token for that game, then they rejoin with the same name and role without being asked for a name.
7. Given a link to a game that does not exist, when it is opened, then a "game not found" page is shown with a link to create a new game.
8. Every player sees each player's online or offline status, and the facilitator is shown separately from voters.
9. Player tokens are generated on the server, stored only as hashes, kept in the browser's `localStorage` (one per game), and never appear in URLs or logs.
10. Games, names and tokens are kept in memory only; nothing is written to disk or a database.
11. Every socket payload and request body is validated with a Zod schema from `src/axon.Shared`; invalid payloads get an error ack and do not change state.

title: Set the story and vote with hidden cards
description:
As a facilitator, I want to set the story we are estimating, and as a voter, I want to pick a card in secret, so that nobody is influenced before the reveal.

Covers the `story:set` and `vote:cast` events, the `waiting` and `voting` phases, the `StoryPanel` and the `CardDeck`.

**Scope:** full-stack.

**Specs:** `requirements.md` Req 3 (all), Req 4 (all); `design.md` sections Game State Machine, Realtime Events, `PublicGameState`, Security.

**Depends on:** Create a game and join it.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Given I am the facilitator and no story is set, when I enter a title (1-200 characters) and an optional link, then the story is shown to every player and voting opens.
2. Given a story link that is not an absolute `http` or `https` URL, when the facilitator submits it, then it is rejected with `INVALID_STORY`.
3. Story links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
4. Given voting is open, when the facilitator edits the title or link, then every player sees the change.
5. Given no story is set, then voters cannot vote.
6. Given voting is open, then a voter can pick one of 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ?, coffee, change it, or withdraw it.
7. Given a voter has voted, then every player sees that this voter has voted, but not the value.
8. Before the reveal, no vote value is sent to any client (verified by an integration test that inspects every `game:state` payload).
9. Given the facilitator sends `vote:cast`, then it is rejected with `FORBIDDEN`.
10. Given a card value that is not in the deck, then it is rejected with `INVALID_CARD`.
11. Given a voter sends `story:set`, then it is rejected with `FORBIDDEN`.
12. The card deck is a keyboard-accessible radio group (arrow keys and Space).

title: Reveal votes with distribution, average, consensus and outliers
description:
As a team, we want to see all votes at the same time with a summary, so that we can discuss the differences.

Covers the `round:reveal` event, the `revealed` phase, `calculateStats` and the `ResultsPanel`.

**Scope:** full-stack.

**Specs:** `requirements.md` Req 5 (all); `design.md` sections Results Calculation (including the example table), `RoundStats`, Vote and Reveal.

**Depends on:** Set the story and vote.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Given voting is open and at least one vote is cast, when the facilitator reveals, then every player sees, within 1 second, each voter's card and the number of votes per card as bars.
2. Given no vote is cast, then the reveal button is disabled and `round:reveal` is rejected with `WRONG_PHASE`.
3. Given a voter sends `round:reveal`, then it is rejected with `FORBIDDEN`.
4. The average uses numeric votes only and is rounded to one decimal; `?` and coffee are shown but excluded.
5. Given at least two numeric votes that are all equal, then consensus is shown.
6. Given numeric votes that differ, then the voters with the lowest and highest vote are highlighted as outliers.
7. Given no numeric votes, then "no average" is shown and no consensus or outliers.
8. Voters who did not vote are shown as "no vote".
9. Given votes are revealed, then `vote:cast` is rejected with `WRONG_PHASE`.
10. `calculateStats` has unit tests for every row of the example table in `design.md` plus: a single numeric vote, only `?`/coffee, ties when suggesting the estimate (higher value wins).
11. The reveal and the consensus result are announced through an `aria-live` region.

title: Re-vote, record the final estimate and keep a session summary
description:
As a facilitator, I want to re-vote or record the agreed estimate and move on, and as a team, we want a summary of what we estimated, so that every round ends with one number we can copy to our backlog.

Covers the `round:revote` and `round:finish` events, the suggested estimate, skipping, the history in `PublicGameState`, `FacilitatorControls` and `SessionSummary`.

**Scope:** full-stack.

**Specs:** `requirements.md` Req 6 (all), Req 7 (all); `design.md` sections Game State Machine, Results Calculation (suggested estimate), `PublicGameState` (history, total).

**Depends on:** Reveal votes.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Given votes are revealed, when the facilitator starts a re-vote, then all votes are cleared, votes are hidden again and the same story stays.
2. Given votes are revealed, then the final estimate field is pre-filled with the consensus value, or the deck value closest to the average (higher one on a tie), or empty if there is no average.
3. Given votes are revealed, when the facilitator records a final estimate from 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 or 21, then the story and estimate are added to the summary and the game returns to waiting for the next story.
4. Given `?` or coffee is sent as a final estimate, then it is rejected.
5. Given voting is open or votes are revealed, when the facilitator skips the story, then it is added to the summary as "skipped" and the game returns to waiting.
6. Given the next story is set, then all votes from the previous round are cleared.
7. Every player sees the summary: stories in the order they were finished, with title, link and estimate or "skipped", and the total of the estimates.
8. Any player can copy the summary as plain text.
9. Given a voter sends `round:revote` or `round:finish`, then it is rejected with `FORBIDDEN`.
10. E2E: a facilitator and three voters play two rounds (one with a re-vote, one skipped) and the summary shows both.

title: Facilitator reconnect and removing players
description:
As a facilitator, I want to keep control of my game when my connection drops and to remove unwanted players, so that the session isn't disrupted.

Covers facilitator offline state, role restoration by token, the `player:remove` / `player:removed` events and banned tokens.

**Scope:** full-stack.

**Specs:** `requirements.md` Req 8 (all); `design.md` sections Join and Reconnect, Data Model (`bannedTokenHashes`), Security.

**Depends on:** Re-vote, record the final estimate.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Given the facilitator disconnects, then the game keeps running and voters see a "facilitator offline" banner.
2. Given the facilitator is offline, then voters can still vote, change and withdraw votes.
3. Given the facilitator is offline, then no other player can reveal, re-vote, finish, skip or change the story (all rejected with `FORBIDDEN`).
4. Given the facilitator reopens the game link in the same browser, then they get the facilitator role back and the banner disappears for everyone.
5. The facilitator role is never passed to another player.
6. Given the facilitator removes a voter, then that voter's vote is discarded, the voter sees "you were removed from this game" and is disconnected, and the other players no longer see them.
7. Given a removed voter tries to rejoin with the same token, then it is rejected with `REMOVED`.
8. Given a voter sends `player:remove`, then it is rejected with `FORBIDDEN`.
9. E2E: the facilitator reloads mid-round and keeps control; a removed voter cannot rejoin.

title: Game lifetime: clean up empty games and handle server restarts
description:
As a team, we want games to disappear after use so that no data is kept, and as an operator, I want memory use to stay bounded.

Covers the sweeper in `GameStore`, the 12-hour cap and `SIGTERM` handling.

**Scope:** full-stack (server sweeper plus the client message when a game ends).

**Specs:** `requirements.md` Req 9 (all); `design.md` section Game Lifetime.

**Depends on:** Facilitator reconnect and removing players.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Given no player has been connected to a game for 2 minutes, then the game is deleted and its link shows "game not found".
2. Given a player reconnects within 2 minutes of the game becoming empty, then the game is kept with its state intact.
3. Given a game is older than 12 hours, then it is deleted whatever its state.
4. Given the server receives `SIGTERM`, then every connected player receives `game:ended` with reason `server-restart` and sees a message that the game ended because the server restarted.
5. The app tells players (for example in the footer or on the create page) that games are temporary and end when the server restarts.
6. Sweeper timing is covered by unit tests with fake timers.

title: Light/dark theme and accessibility pass
description:
As a player, I want light or dark mode and an accessible interface so that the app is comfortable for everyone.

Covers `ThemeToggle`, Tailwind `dark:` styles and automated accessibility checks.

**Scope:** frontend (plus E2E tests).

**Specs:** `requirements.md` Req 10 (all) and the Accessibility non-functional requirement; `design.md` section Front End (Styling, Accessibility).

**Depends on:** Reveal votes (all main views exist).
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Given a first visit, then the theme follows the operating system's light or dark setting.
2. When a player switches the theme, then the choice applies immediately and is remembered in their browser on the next visit.
3. Both themes meet WCAG 2.1 AA colour contrast.
4. All interactive elements (cards, buttons, forms, copy link, remove player) are reachable and usable with the keyboard, with a visible focus indicator.
5. Vote status changes, the reveal and the consensus result are announced to screen readers.
6. `@axe-core/playwright` reports no serious or critical violations on the create, join, voting and revealed views, in both themes.

title: Rate limiting, Docker image and load smoke test
description:
As an operator, I want the app protected against abuse and packaged for deployment so that it can run reliably on one server.

Covers REST and socket rate limits, CORS lock-down, the Docker image and a load smoke test.

**Scope:** full-stack (server hardening plus deployment).

**Specs:** `requirements.md` non-functional requirements (Real time, Scale, Security, Privacy); `design.md` sections Security, Architecture (single instance).

**Depends on:** Game lifetime.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Given one IP creates games or checks game IDs too fast, then `POST /api/games` and `GET /api/games/:id/exists` return `429` and the client shows a friendly message.
2. Given one socket sends more than about 10 events per second, then extra events are rejected with `RATE_LIMITED` and the game state is not changed.
3. The number of socket connections per IP is limited.
4. Socket.IO and REST only accept the app's own origin (CORS).
5. Logs contain only the game ID and event names: no player names, story text or tokens (checked by a test).
6. A Dockerfile builds a production image that serves the front end and the server on one port; `docker run` starts the app and `/healthz` returns `200`.
7. A load smoke script runs 100 games with 20 sockets each against one instance, and state changes reach every player within 1 second at p95.
